# GST FAQ for Reimbursements (FIN-GST-02)

## Introduction
Goods and Services Tax changes how a reimbursement is recorded. A claim is not
merely a payment back to the employee — where the invoice is raised correctly,
Aarohi Logistics Pvt Ltd can also recover the tax as **input tax credit**. This
note explains what Finance needs to make that happen.

## What makes an invoice claimable
An invoice supports input tax credit only when it names the supplier's GSTIN,
names Aarohi Logistics and *our* GSTIN as the recipient, carries the HSN or SAC
code, and states CGST, SGST, IGST or cess separately from the taxable value. A
hotel folio made out to the employee personally does not qualify, which is why
the **Leave and Expense Policy** (HR-LEX-07) requires a GST-compliant invoice
above ₹500.

## The place-of-supply trap
The single most common error is charging IGST where CGST plus SGST was due, or
the reverse. Hotel accommodation is taxed where the property stands, so a
Bengaluru employee staying in Pune receives a Maharashtra invoice, and Aarohi
Logistics can claim that credit only against a Maharashtra registration. Where
we hold no registration in that state, the tax is a cost and the claim should be
filed on the gross amount.

## Why the Travel Desk matters
Because place of supply and the recipient GSTIN have to be right at the moment
of booking, and not corrected afterwards, bookings go through the **Travel
Desk**. The desk holds our state-wise GSTIN list and passes the correct one to
the vendor. The booking procedure and the escalation path are set out in the
*Travel Desk Handbook* (OPS-TD-11). Meera Iyer, the Finance Controller, signs
off any exception to this route.
